---
title: "Earth2Studio.jl"
---

## Overview

**Earth2Studio.jl** is a thin Julia wrapper around [NVIDIA's earth2studio](https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2studio) Python package for AI-powered weather and climate forecasting. It uses [PythonCall.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPy/PythonCall.jl) to expose the full `earth2studio` Python API — data sources, prognostic and diagnostic models, perturbations, IO backends, run workflows, and verification statistics — as Python objects you can call from Julia.

The package itself is intentionally minimal: it imports `earth2studio` and its top-level submodules and holds them as `Py` references. Nothing is exported, because upstream names such as `run` and `io` would clash with `Base`. All functionality lives in the upstream Python package.

## Quickstart

Install Earth2Studio.jl:

```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/RallypointOne/Earth2Studio.jl")
```

On first load, [CondaPkg.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPy/CondaPkg.jl) creates a Conda environment with Python (3.11–3.13), `earth2studio[data]` (version 0.18 or newer), and the conda-forge packages the data sources need. No manual pip step is required. Model extras are opt-in — add a `CondaPkg.toml` to your own project and CondaPkg merges it with the one shipped here:

```toml
[pip.deps.earth2studio]
extras = ["fcn", "pangu"]
```

Then call into the Python API through the module:

```julia
using Earth2Studio
using Dates

ds = Earth2Studio.data.ARCO()
da = ds(DateTime(2023, 6, 15), ["t2m", "u10m"])

model   = Earth2Studio.models.px.FCN.load_model(Earth2Studio.models.px.FCN.load_default_package())
backend = Earth2Studio.io.ZarrBackend("/tmp/forecast.zarr")
Earth2Studio.run.deterministic([DateTime(2023, 6, 15)], 10, model, ds, backend)
```

`DateTime` and `String` convert to the Python types earth2studio expects, and Julia vectors are accepted wherever earth2studio iterates over a list. See the [Tutorial](tutorial.qmd) for the full set of interop patterns.
